caption:
Apple plans to bring Apple Intelligence to mainland China in December with iOS 27.3, Bloomberg reported.
Basic tools like Writing Tools and Clean Up are coming, but the new Siri AI and Image Playground are not.
Alibaba's models power it, with a filter that lets the government approve model updates.

Would you use an iPhone AI that a government signs off on?

slides.headline: Apple Intelligence is finally coming to China. But *Siri AI* is not invited

slides.heading: A *December* launch
paras: Apple plans to launch Apple Intelligence in mainland China in December as part of iOS 27.3, Bloomberg reported. Apple has not announced a date.
The features first arrived with iOS 18.1 in 2024, but they have been unavailable in China since then because of regulatory hurdles.

slides.heading: What Chinese users *get*
paras: The launch reportedly includes basic features such as Writing Tools, notification summaries and Clean Up in Photos, which removes unwanted objects from images.
Some text generation tools will be limited in certain apps, according to Bloomberg.

slides.heading: What's *missing*
paras: The new Siri AI assistant is not included, and neither are Apple's image generation tools such as Image Playground.

paras.t: Bloomberg's Mark Gurman said Apple executives have little optimism that Siri AI will reach China soon.

slides.heading: *Alibaba* inside the iPhone
paras: China restricts foreign AI, so Apple partnered with Alibaba, whose Qwen and Tongyi Wanxiang models were cleared for iPhones. Baidu works with Apple on search and Siri features.
Alibaba provides a filter that lets the government approve ongoing model updates, 9to5Mac reported, citing Bloomberg.

slides.hook: Huawei, Xiaomi and Oppo already offer AI features in China. Follow to see if Apple can catch up.
